correctness.rationale: The shared-pressure reduction is exact: at an interior equilibrium h_{u,v}(x1)=h_{u,v}(x2)=L(S), with h(z)=z/(1-z)-uz-vz^2 and L(S)>=0. For u<1, h prime has a unique interior minimum when v>1; its value 3v^(2/3)-2v-u changes sign exactly at t^2(3-2t)=u. At equality h remains strictly increasing. For u>=1, Q(z)=1/(1-z)-u-vz is strictly convex and each positive level of h=zQ is attained at most once; the zero-pressure e=f=1 case and physical-square boundaries are handled separately. The two-preimage construction supplies admissible parameters for every strict supercritical pair. The exact rational witness and 324 Fraction identities support the reduction but are not used as the all-parameter proof.
residual_risks: The proof depends on the stated equal-community deterministic mean-field equations and admissible nonnegative assortativity; no unequal-community, stochastic finite-network, stability, or global-convergence claim follows.

value.rationale: The motivating question is which physically meaningful pair/triangle reinforcement strengths can support different stationary opinions in otherwise symmetric communities. The theorem gives a sharp universal obstruction over a natural continuous parameter family and a constructive converse, explaining why triangle assortativity changes the published phase diagrams. It is a structural all-parameter result, not a numerical slice or a stability claim.
residual_risks: Value is confined to equal-sized deterministic mean-field communities and does not imply stability, basin size, or finite-network behavior.
